newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index leaps in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index leaps in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index leaped 163 points to 13,895 shortly after the start of trading on Wednesday morning, prompted by the U.S. Federal Reserve chief's upbeat comments and a positive outlook for local property stocks, brokers said.
Turnover was a hefty HK$2.35 billion.

"Greenspan's (comments) saying there is no fear of inflation and interest rate hikes is a positive injection into the U.S. and Hong Kong markets," said Peter Lai, associate director of OCBC Securities.

U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan told the U.S. Senate Budget Committee on Tuesday that the U.S. economy showed vigour but indicated there were few signs of imbalances or inflationary tensions associated with past economic expansions.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average vaulted 40.03 points to 6,883.90, its 10th record close of 1997.
"I expect the index to test 14,000 today," said Lai. "Probably with gains in interest-rate sensitive property stocks and banks."

Brokers also said the index's leap was due to gains in Cheung Kong and Hutchison, following the announcement of the group's successful tender for the last phase of a large residential estate at Tung Chung, which lies next to Hong Kong's new international airport on Chep Lap Kok.
Hutchison Whampoa, the second most actively traded issue, jumped HK$2.00 to HK$65.25 on trade of HK$141.20 million. Cheung Kong gained HK$1.50 to HK$76.25 on turnover of HK$94.16 million.
International banking giant HSBC Holdings put on HK$1.50 to HK$182.00 and Hang Seng added HK$0.75 to HK$94.75.

Wheelock International topped the most active table with turnover of HK$1.27 billion. A block of 50 million shares was traded at HK$22.80 at the market opening. The share fell HK$1.085 to HK$22.80 in early trade.
The technical picture, which looked mixed prior to the market's strong opening, has turned around, chartists said.
"As long as the market holds above 13,700 on high turnover, the index will retest 14,000 and higher," said Charles Cheung, executive director at J&A Securities.
